description: Behaviour evals — the skill explains a failed or stalled objective from its state files, writes diagnosis.md, and hands off to exactly one next command without changing state.

evals.name: worker-returned-without-handoff
evals.prompt: Objective auth-system stalled. task-002 is still 'running' in .dev-files/objectives/auth-system/tasks/task-002.json but there is no handoffs/task-002.json, and the other two tasks have completed handoffs. Why did it stall and what do I run next?
evals.expected_output: The skill runs scripts/objective-timeline.sh on the objective directory first, reports first_cause worker-stopped-without-handoff for task-002 (invariant 6: no handoff means the task is failed, never completed), writes .dev-files/objectives/auth-system/diagnosis.md with the timeline, first cause, evidence and next command, and recommends exactly one command: /switch-dev handoff objective=auth-system task-002 if the task worktree has uncommitted work, otherwise /worker-dev auth-system task-002.
expectations: The skill runs objective-timeline.sh before reading any file by hand
The report names worker-stopped-without-handoff (or rate-limit-death when a rate-limit record exists) for task-002 as the first cause
The report cites tasks/task-002.json and the absence of handoffs/task-002.json as evidence
Exactly one next command is given, and it is /switch-dev handoff or /worker-dev, never /orchestrate-dev
The skill does NOT run task-set, set-status, or write a handoff itself
diagnosis.md is written under the objective directory and nothing else is written

evals.name: completed-without-validation-then-integrated
evals.prompt: Diagnose objective payments-v2. It was marked integrating but the integrated branch is broken. One handoff says completed with validation: [] and another says partial but its task is marked completed.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports two findings — completed-without-validation (a claim with no evidence) and integrated-around-partial (critical) — picks the earlier high-severity one as first cause, explains from the handoff summaries what each worker actually did, and recommends /orchestrate-dev payments-v2 to decide (re-plan, drop or narrow) before re-integrating. It quotes the handoff files as evidence and does not guess at test results that were never recorded.
expectations: Both completed-without-validation and integrated-around-partial appear in All findings
The first cause is justified by timestamp and severity, not by which finding sounds worse
The report quotes the partial handoff's summary when explaining the mechanism
The next command is /orchestrate-dev payments-v2 — a planning/integration problem is never handed to /worker-dev
The empty validation[] is described as missing evidence, never as 'probably passed'

evals.name: no-git-fallback-and-clean-objective
evals.prompt: Run diagnose-objective on objective docs-refresh. This machine has no git binary available, and the objective looks fine to me — I just want the report.
evals.expected_output: The skill still runs the script (git.available is false), reports no findings, writes diagnosis.md whose Evidence section states that the integration-lag and dirty-worktree checks were skipped because git is unavailable (degraded, not silently reported as 'not behind'), and gives the status-dependent next command: nothing if the objective is completed, otherwise /orchestrate-dev docs-refresh to integrate or resume.
expectations: The script runs and the skill does not refuse because git is unavailable
The Evidence section explicitly says the git-dependent checks were not run (fallback named, not hidden)
No failure class is invented for a clean objective
The next command follows objective.status: 'nothing' for completed/abandoned, /orchestrate-dev otherwise
The chat reply is two sentences plus the next command and the diagnosis.md path, not the full timeline
